issues.failure_explanation: The space is defined to contain v with gamma_1 v in H^{-1/2}(Gamma), but its norm uses the L^2(Gamma) norm of gamma_1 v, which is not defined for a general element of H^{-1/2}(Gamma). Thus H^1(omega,Gamma) is not well-defined as a normed space.

failure_location.quote:
which is equipped by the natural norm
\[
\left\Vert \bullet\right\Vert _{H^1(\omega,\Gamma)}:=\sqrt{\left\Vert \bullet\right\Vert
_{H^{1}\left(  \omega\right)  }^{2}+\left\Vert \gamma_{1}\bullet\right\Vert
_{L^{2}\left(  \Gamma\right)  }^{2}}.
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose a consistent space: either require gamma_1 v in L^2(Gamma) and adjust the subspace claim, or keep gamma_1 v in H^{-1/2}(Gamma) and use the H^{-1/2} norm. For the stated theorem, the latter is intended.
issues.overall_effect: The meaning of H^1(Omega,S_R) in Theorem thm:C_Friedrich and Corollary CorTrace is ambiguous, and the proof of thm:C_Friedrich uses an L^2 normal derivative while the statement uses H^{-1/2}.
issues.title: Ill-defined norm for H^1(omega,Gamma)
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the norm (or membership) fixes the definition; the main mathematical content is preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: For n=2, the mode (0,0) contributes an imaginary part bounded by c_2+|Im s|, not by |Im s|. The proof drops the constant c_2 and claims a bound by |Im s| ||g||_{L^2}^2, which is false for small |Im s| and nonzero constant component of g.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Include the c_2 term for the (0,0) mode and bound it by C(n)||g||_{H^{1/2}}^2.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of item (iv) of Theorem thm:DtN is invalid for n=2, although the stated theorem remains true.
issues.title: Imaginary-part bound in DtN proof drops constant-mode term
issues.why_classification: A short local correction to the proof restores the argument without changing the theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: H is defined as the union over z in C_{\geq0} of the subspaces {v : partial_r v = DtN(z)v}. This union is not closed under addition, so it is not a vector space and hence not a Hilbert space. The weak convergence argument and the claim that the weak limit u lies in H are invalid.

failure_location.quote:
consider the Hilbert space
\[
H=\left\{  v\in H^{1}\left(  \Omega,S_{R}\right)  \mid\partial_{r}
v-\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  z\right)  v=0\ \text{ on }S_{R}\text{ for some
}z\in\mathbb{C}_{\geq0}\right\}  .
\]
(The completeness of $H$ follows from the continuity of the
$\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  s\right)  $ operator by \Cref{thm:DtN}.)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace H by a closed subspace for a fixed z, or work with a sequence v_k with corresponding z_k, show z_k is bounded, and pass to the limit.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:C_Friedrich is invalid; the Friedrichs inequality and Corollary CorTrace are unsupported as written.
issues.title: H is not a Hilbert space in the proof of Friedrichs inequality
issues.why_classification: The main theorem's proof needs a nontrivial repair of its compactness argument, but the statement remains true and a contained argument can fix it.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem's inequality measures the normal derivative in H^{-1/2}(S_R), but the contradiction sequence assumes convergence in L^2(S_R). If H^1(Omega,S_R) only requires the normal derivative in H^{-1/2}(S_R), this stronger assumption does not cover all sequences violating the stated inequality.

failure_location.quote:
Assume for a contradiction to (\ref{eqn:C_F}) that there exists a sequence
$(v_{k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\subset H$ with $\left\Vert v_{k}\right\Vert
_{L^{2}\left(  \Omega\right)  }=1$ for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\Vert\nabla
v_{k}\Vert_{L^{2}\left(  \Omega\right)  }+\left\Vert \partial_{r}
v_{k}\right\Vert _{L^{2}\left(  S_{R}\right)  }\rightarrow0$ as $k\rightarrow
\infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the H^{-1/2}(S_R) norm in the contradiction sequence and adapt the compactness argument accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:C_Friedrich does not establish the stated H^{-1/2} version of the Friedrichs inequality.
issues.title: Friedrichs proof uses L^2 instead of H^{-1/2} normal derivative
issues.why_classification: A nontrivial but contained modification of the contradiction argument is needed to cover the stated norm.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Consider a bounded
Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ in $n\geq3$ dimensions such
that $S_{R}\subset\partial\Omega$ is relatively closed in $\partial\Omega$.

issues.failure_explanation: CorTrace applies Theorem thm:C_Friedrich to Omega, which requires S_R subset partial Omega. The corollary only assumes S_R is relatively closed in partial omega for some omega subset Omega, which does not imply S_R subset partial Omega.

failure_location.quote:
Consider a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$,
$n\geq3$ and let $C_{\operatorname*{F}}$ be as in \Cref{thm:C_Friedrich}. 
Any $v\in H^{1}\left(  \Omega\right)  $ with the
properties
\[
\begin{array}
[c]{cl}
\left.  \left(  -\Delta v+s^{2}v\right)  \right\vert _{\omega}=0 & \text{for
some }\omega\subset\Omega\text{ such that }S_{R}\text{ is a relatively closed
subset of }\partial\omega,\\
\partial_{r}v=\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  s\right)    v   &

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that S_R subset partial Omega is relatively closed in partial Omega.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary is not proved as stated; it needs the additional hypothesis S_R subset partial Omega.
issues.title: CorTrace missing hypothesis S_R subset partial Omega
issues.why_classification: Adding the intended boundary hypothesis is a local fix and preserves the main application.

issues.failure_explanation: The H^1 norm in spherical coordinates includes the angular derivative term with coefficient lambda_m = m(m+n-2), not m^2. Since lambda_m >= m^2, the displayed norm underestimates the true H^1 norm, so bounding it does not establish continuity in H^1_loc.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace m^2 by lambda_m = m(m+n-2) in H_{m,j}^2 and adjust the estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The continuity proof for the series solution in Proposition PropProblems.2a is incomplete.
issues.title: Incorrect angular derivative norm in PropProblems proof
issues.why_classification: A local replacement of the angular coefficient fixes the norm and the subsequent estimates can be adjusted routinely.

issues.failure_explanation: For m=0 and nu=0 (n=2), the right-hand side is zero, but F_{0,j}^2 = integral_R^d r dr > 0. Thus the displayed estimate is false. The preceding estimates for F_{m,j}^2 are also incorrect for n=2nu+2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the estimates for F^2, G^2, H^2 and the final max bound, including a positive term for the constant mode.
